I don't usually plug shit but filet knives can be really important. I bought one of those WorkSharp belt sharpeners about 6 years ago and I'm never going back.

I've got it all. Arkansas wetstones, diamond ones, fixed mount lansky crap, ceramic rods, the ones with wheels, the carbide rods and a dozen of those pull through bastards. With enough time I can put a razor edge on ONE knife with a good wetstone........after two or three attempts. And it's GOOD.

With that little belt sander it's a hell of an edge EVERY TIME.......with all my knives in two minutes. Not as good but damn close.

It's worth the $80 and it's rare that I say that about anything.

I've always used a wetstone and the bottom of a coffee mug. a minute or 2 to clean up any burrs after each use is all I've ever needed. The belt sander seems like a good idea for neglected knives though which I do have a couple of. Them pull through things always end up in the bottoms of my tackle boxes and never get touched.
What did you use for bait? Some good catches there. I'd fish a lot more often if I were successful like that.

A silver spinner and a worm is what works in this pond, this is a series of 3 stocked ponds, they are named lake 34, 35 and 36. 34 and 35 they are bug eaters but 36 they only eat minnows.

Here's a tip for stocked trout ponds, probably works for any stocked fish. But stocked fish are raised in basically swimming pools, and to them from egg to the day they are stocked food is brown pellets that fall from the sky, they don't have the hunting instinct they'd normally develop as tiny fry feeding on tiny bugs. So once they ae stocked into lakes and ponds they pretty much near starve because they don't understand food, they learn to eat the most abundant food source they come accross and unless they near starve again don't venture off of that initial food source they find.

The best way to find out how to fish a specific pond or lake is to scout it out, watch it in mid day on a calm day and see if the surface is crawling with bug, check again at dusk to see if little minnows start jumping, even through a minnow trap into it full of petstore fish food, and see if the trap some up full of minnows or bugs or crawfish or even snails, if you don't have a minnow trap check youtube for how to make one from a 2l bottle. You'll never understand a stocked pond the first time out there, but you might get lucky and brong the rght bait for trout almost trout, rainbows browns brooks I use a silver or yellow and black spinner as my staple usually silver, and then the bait of choice on the hook. a small sinker helps you don't need to go deep though unless you're after lake trout.

Also this was only 2 and a half hours of fishing. We had a lot more action too, my son more then me, he had 3 more get off right at the canoe, and almost always had a fish nibbling on his worms. He caught the biggest one too(not by much), but I caught more, I landed 4 he landed 3. He used a pretty standard sized spinner and a large worm hook, I used a micro spinner, with a tiny hook by comparisson and I only used half worms, he used full.

For trout all we can fish are the stocked ponds, the season is closed for the naturals which get much larger, I wouldn;t even keep naurals this size usually unless they are hooked bad.
